newsitem.title: GREECE: VIRGIN'S BRANSON SAYS MONOPOLY IS BAD BUSINESS.
newsitem.headline: VIRGIN'S BRANSON SAYS MONOPOLY IS BAD BUSINESS.

text.p: The owner of the Virgin group of companies, Richard Branson, talked about monopoly, competition and privatisation at a meeting organised by the Greek Foundation for Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE), in Athens.
Branson said that monopoly concerns the concentration of power and it is not simply an economic matter.
"Most monopolies are government creations and rely on government protection for their continued existence," Branson said.
There are no areas of state monopoly that could not be eliminated and replaced by creative ways of privatising.
"The failures of privatisation have all stemmed from being too timid, from not going far enough and not introducing real competition right away. The big lesson is: It pays to be bold," he said.
With regard to Greece, Branson said that up to now it has not attracted too much foreign investor interest.
However, it is best to be innovative. That is why he has opened up businesses in Greece before anyone else, he said.
His aim is to provide better quality than existing rivals in the market.
In Athens he has established two Virgin Megastores. These offer a higher quality service than big Greek record stores, he said.

Branson has initiated some of Virgin Airlines' routes in Greece. Taking into account the status of his main competitor, Greece's state carrier Olympic Airways, he has aimed at providing better quality at low prices.

"The EU is as big as the United States and can be as powerful. We can now create in Europe, companies as big as those formed in the U.S.," Branson said. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
